records.adversarial_note: The raw ingredient of C1 (per-model refusal response to a push along the harm direction) is computed in 2507.11878 on 3 models and differs visibly across them, but only as a mechanism contrast (harm vs refusal direction), in behavioural refusal-rate units at chosen layers, not as a finite-difference gain on a late refusal-axis projection and never used to compare models' safety. 2606.08044 LVS is the only published per-model CAUSAL sensitivity score used as a safety indicator across model variants (Table 1), but its perturbation is undirected (not along the model's own harm direction), it needs generation + a safety classifier, and it is explicitly positioned against, not validated by, behavioural benchmarks. records.adversarial_note: Closest to PUBLISHED of the five. Report 74 ranks 16 models by a directional-ablation outcome and correlates it with a jailbreak benchmark (null result), which is C2's cross-model design in generic form; it is kept at ADJACENT only because (i) it is a non-peer-reviewed org report, (ii) its quantity is a behavioural success fraction of third-party weight abliteration (method 'advanced' dominates) rather than a refusal-MARGIN drop from removing the model's own direction in a layer band, (iii) there is no benign-twin (over-refusal) arm and no anisotropy-matched random-direction control. Arditi's 13-model Figure 1 is computed per model but treated as mechanism evidence (all models collapse), not as a safety ranking. If reviewers treat Report 74 as publication, C2's claim must be narrowed to the two-sided, random-controlled, margin-based form, and the null rho = -0.003 must be cited as prior evidence against a positive result.
records.positioning_sentence: Directional ablation removes refusal in every one of 13 chat models (arXiv:2406.11717), and a practitioner report found abliteration resistance uncorrelated with jailbreak refusal across 16 models (Failure-First Report 74, rho = -0.003); our self-ablation sensitivity differs by measuring a margin drop on both harmful items and benign twins relative to an anisotropy-matched random direction, and by testing it against harmful-refusal and over-refusal benchmarks across held-out families.

records.adversarial_note: Jorak is the nearest functional relative: reference-free, weights-only, reads o_proj/down_proj against the refusal axis, used to classify models. Differences: its main statistic is direction-agnostic (shared least-gain singular vector across layers) and binary-thresholded to detect a SEVERED write (r^T W ~ 0); C4 z-scores the write capacity along the model's own refusal axis against random directions from the layer's output span and is intended as a GRADED safety score correlated with benchmarks. Because a z-score of ||r^T W|| near the floor is exactly Jorak's 'severed' condition, a reviewer could call C4 'Jorak made continuous'; the paper must cite it and claim only the graded, benchmark-validated, cross-family use. Iteration-1's adversarial pass (raw/adversarial_C3_C4_C5.json, its C4 = weights-only parent-free graded edit strength) stayed STILL-OPEN, and its abliteration.org wiki concession ('A truly novel benchmark should test whether method can be recovered from candidate weights alone, without an attested base') still applies; Jorak (created 2026-07-24) post-dates part of that search and was not in iter-1's excluded list, so it narrows that verdict.
records.positioning_sentence: Reference-free weight signatures of refusal-writing matrices are already used to flag abliterated checkpoints (Jorak, github.com/JolanMc/Jorak; cf. the base-anchored audit of arXiv:2607.01854), so our contribution is not the weight read itself but its use as a graded, random-direction-calibrated writer-capacity score validated against harmful-refusal and over-refusal benchmarks across held-out families.

records.adversarial_note: No source computes a bilinear harm-direction -> refusal-direction gain through attention-output and MLP weight paths summed over depth, per model, let alone ranks models by it. Nearest misses are weight-activation hybrids (2604.27401's c_n uses W_down but multiplies it by a measured perturbation response, and its cross-model predictor FFN/Skip is activation-based and predicts an internal ablation effect, not a benchmark) and circuit papers (2609.00051) that intervene rather than read weights. Citation hop: 2604.27401 found via forward citations of 2406.11717 (raw/A_cites_filtered.txt); its cited concurrent work (Unit42 perturbation-probing note) was checked in iter-1 (CSA note) and does not compute a weight path. Iteration-1's weights-only verdict applies: nothing weights-only is graded against benchmarks.
records.positioning_sentence: Component-level refusal attributions exist (arXiv:2406.11717) and weight-derived neuron couplings have been used to predict ablation effects across 13 models (arXiv:2604.27401), but to our knowledge no prior work reads a harm-to-refusal gain directly from attention-output and MLP weight paths and tests it as a cross-family safety score.

kill_check.why_it_misses_or_closes: No arXiv or peer-reviewed paper reports a per-model harm-to-refusal CAUSAL quantity (harm-direction steering gain, own-direction ablation sensitivity, twin patching, or weight-path gain) and correlates or ranks it against a safety benchmark across models/families. Report 74 does the cross-model correlation, but with third-party executed abliteration success (behavioural, no harm-direction, no over-refusal arm) and is grey literature; LVS is a causal per-model safety score but uses undirected perturbations and reports no benchmark correlation; Arditi (13 models), Zhao (3 models), HRCI (anchors + one trajectory), 2609.03887 (3 models x 3 methods, steering ASR) compute causal quantities per model only as mechanism evidence. AMS 2608.05578 sigma is a non-causal Cohen's-d separation (Pearson r = -0.546 vs JailbreakBench compliance; confirmed: AMS text says 'AMS measures existing direction vectors at scan time', no intervention); RAS 2606.25750 is a non-causal refusal-direction alignment score needing a reference model and family calibration; 2608.13329 concerns prompt-dependence of probe scores (non-causal).
kill_check.residual_novel_scope: (1) the quantity is causal AND keyed to the model's own cross-fitted harm direction (not undirected, not third-party abliteration); (2) parent-free, ~16-prompt budget; (3) two-sided target (harmful-refusal AND over-refusal, blanket refuser must lose); (4) cross-family held-out validation; (5) anisotropy-matched random-direction controls.
kill_check.required_positioning_sentence: Causal refusal interventions have so far been reported per model as mechanism evidence (arXiv:2406.11717; arXiv:2507.11878; arXiv:2606.16349), per-unit latent-perturbation sensitivity has been proposed as a safety score without benchmark validation (arXiv:2606.08044), and a practitioner report found abliteration resistance uncorrelated with jailbreak refusal across 16 models (Failure-First Report 74, rho = -0.003); we are the first to test, parent-free and with ~16 prompts, whether causal harm-to-refusal quantities keyed to each model's own harm direction track both harmful-refusal and over-refusal benchmarks across held-out architecture families.
